_about: NC Envirothon in the class platform's unit shape (DESIGN_class_platform_2026-10-28.md §4.1, §11; PR 3 CPUNIT). The CARDS stay in ONE place, envirothon/nc_envirothon_unit.json (cards.from), and the compiled file stays envirothon.js (build.file, built by envirothon/build_envirothon_js.py) with window.HoweEnvirothon as the alias of HoweUnits.nc_envirothon — so nothing is copied twice. Section keys are today's station ids and deck keys are unchanged. Run: node units/build/compile_unit.js nc_envirothon
title: NC Envirothon
desc: The five NC Envirothon stations — Forestry, Soils and Land Use, Aquatic Ecology, Wildlife, Current Environmental Issues — plus the general science concepts, every card straight from the official 2026–27 study documents.

rules._why: 110 fronts hold . or / — the app saves their backs under the coded key (mastDefKey, ENVUNIT); a card's class-layer key is its order, never its front

items.name: Diameter tape (d-tape)
items.use: Wraps around a tree at breast height to read the tree’s diameter
items.src: Forestry Manual p.63

items.name: Biltmore stick
items.use: Held 25 inches from your eye to measure a tree’s diameter, and its height from 66 feet away
items.src: Forestry Manual p.63–65; 2022 Area 8 Forestry Q16

items.name: Clinometer
items.use: Measures how tall a tree is — the most-used height tool, small and held in one hand
items.src: Forestry Manual p.65

items.name: Abney level
items.use: Measures tree height and the slope of the ground, but needs adjusting now and then
items.src: Forestry Manual p.65

items.name: Increment borer
items.use: Screwed into a living tree to pull out a thin core of wood for counting its rings
items.src: Forestry Manual p.66; 2026 Area 8 Forestry Q19–20

items.name: Wedge prism
items.use: A thin wedge of glass you look through to decide which trees to count in a timber cruise
items.src: Forestry Manual p.67

items.name: Caliper
items.use: Two arms that close on a tree or log to measure its diameter — used on odd-shaped or cut trees
items.src: Glossary p.5; Forestry Manual p.63

items.name: Chain (66-ft tape)
items.use: Measures distance on the ground: one chain is 66 feet
items.src: Forestry Manual p.62

items.name: Secchi disc
items.use: Lowered into a lake until it disappears, to see how deep light reaches (how clear the water is)
items.src: Aquatics Manual p.62; 2021 Area 8 Aquatics Q5

items.name: D-net
items.use: Scoops bugs off the bottom, banks and plants of a stream — it is made for moving water, not for catching fish
items.src: 2022 Area 8 Aquatics Q14–15 (Aquatic Sampling Guide p.4)

items.name: Kick net
items.use: Held across a riffle while someone kicks the rocks just upstream, so the current washes bugs into the net
items.src: Field practice, not yet in the MS study documents (check: Aquatic Sampling Equipment handout)

items.name: Surber sampler
items.use: A frame set on a shallow riffle (under 1 foot deep) to collect the bugs from one square foot of stream bottom
items.src: Field practice, not yet in the MS study documents (check: Aquatic Sampling Equipment handout)

items.name: Eckman dredge
items.use: Grabs a scoop of bottom mud, and the animals living in it, from a lake or pond
items.src: 2022 Area 8 Aquatics Q16 (Aquatic Sampling Guide p.5)

items.name: Seine
items.use: A long net pulled through the water by two people to catch fish quickly
items.src: 2021 Area 8 Aquatics Q5, Q19 (Equipment List p.9–11)

items.name: Dip net
items.use: A long-handled net for scooping animals from the edge of a pond or slow water
items.src: Field practice, not yet in the MS study documents (check: Aquatic Sampling Equipment handout)

items.name: Plankton net
items.use: A cone of very fine mesh towed through the water to collect plankton
items.src: 2026 Area 8 Aquatics Q12 (Birge plankton net); Aquatics Manual p.66

items.name: Water sampling bottle
items.use: Closes at a chosen depth to bring up water from that depth for testing
items.src: Field practice, not yet in the MS study documents (check: Aquatic Sampling Equipment handout) (2021 Area 8 Aquatics Q5 lists it)

items.name: Price AA flow meter
items.use: Cups that spin on a measuring rod to measure how fast the water is flowing
items.src: Aquatics Manual p.63

skills._about: 🪲 CPITEMBIOTIC (2026-10-29; RESEARCH_envirothon_skills_2026-10-28.md §4.3, ranked #2 in §5). The 29 kinds and their groups are the NC Guide to Macroinvertebrate Taxa Groups (the guide the 2026 Area 8 key cites; the same as the 29 “· pollution tolerance group” cards); × 3 / 2 / 1 and the ranges are the Aquatics Manual p.62. Count KINDS (taxa), not animals, as the manual card says (“Multiply the number of taxa in each group by its index value”). `like` = the picture question's look-alike lures, by body shape from the guide's descriptions (a choice of lures, not a fact). `replaces` = the 8 biotic-index fact cards of the research's §8.1 — for the trim, which is always the teacher's tap.

skills.label: Label the soil profile
skills._about: 🏷 CPITEMLABEL (2026-10-29; RESEARCH_envirothon_skills_2026-10-28.md §4.8, §4.10, §8.1): our own drawing of a soil pit face. replaces = the research's one card (O horizon · position); every horizon term card stays.

parts.label: O horizon
parts.words: The top layer (when there is one): leaves, needles, twigs, moss and lichens

parts.label: A horizon
parts.words: Topsoil: darker than the layers below (more organic matter), often the most fertile

parts.label: E horizon
parts.words: Light colored or bleached: the zone of eluviation, where clay, iron and humus are lost

parts.label: B horizon
parts.words: Subsoil: the zone of accumulation (illuviation) of what washed down from the A and E

parts.label: C horizon
parts.words: The transition layer between soil and parent material, less weathered

parts.label: R horizon
parts.words: Bedrock

skills.label: Label the lake zones
skills._about: 🏷 CPITEMLABEL (2026-10-29; RESEARCH §4.8): our own drawing of a lake in cross-section (2022 Aquatics Q10, the benthic zone). The yellow dashes mark how far down the sunlight reaches.

parts.label: Riparian zone
parts.words: On or near the bank: the land and plants influenced by the water next to them

parts.label: Littoral zone
parts.words: The shallow, nutrient-rich area near the shore, with rooted plants and abundant life

parts.label: Limnetic zone
parts.words: The open water away from shore, down as far as the sunlight reaches

parts.label: Profundal zone
parts.words: The deepest zone, beneath the limnetic zone, where no light reaches

parts.label: Benthic zone
parts.words: The bottom of a water body

skills.label: Label the groundwater
skills._about: 🏷 CPITEMLABEL (2026-10-29; RESEARCH §4.8: water table / aquifer, 2021 Aquatics Q13 'point to the water table'): our own drawing. The zone of saturation is drawn in the soil just under the water table and the aquifer as the gravel layer the well draws from, the way the Aquatics manual's cards word them.

parts.label: Recharge area
parts.words: The land the water passes down through into an aquifer

parts.label: Unsaturated zone
parts.words: The drier zone above the water table, where the pores hold air as well as water

parts.label: Water table
parts.words: The surface of the zone of saturation: the boundary with the drier, unsaturated zone above it

parts.label: Zone of saturation
parts.words: A zone deeper in the soil where most of the pores are filled with water

parts.label: Aquifer
parts.words: A layer of porous, water-saturated sand, gravel or fractured bedrock that groundwater flows through (a well draws from it)

parts.label: Impermeable layer
parts.words: A layer whose pores are not connected, so groundwater cannot move through it

skills.label: Label the fish
skills._about: 🏷 CPITEMLABEL (2026-10-29; RESEARCH §4.8: fish outside, 2021 Aquatics Q12 the caudal fin): our own drawing of a trout. Five fins have no card in the unit; their words are the plain meaning (dorsal = back, caudal = tail), with no src.

parts.label: Dorsal fin
parts.words: The large fin on the fish's back

parts.label: Adipose fin
parts.words: A tiny, rounded fin between the dorsal fin and the tail fin, on some fish (like the rainbow trout)

parts.label: Caudal fin
parts.words: The tail fin

parts.label: Anal fin
parts.words: The single fin on the belly, near the tail

parts.label: Pelvic fin
parts.words: The paired fins on the belly, about halfway along

parts.label: Pectoral fin
parts.words: The paired fins just behind the gill cover

parts.label: Operculum
parts.words: The gill cover

parts.label: Lateral line
parts.words: A line of sensing cells along the side, from the gill cover to the tail fin, that senses vibrations and temperature changes

skills.label: Label the tree's layers
skills._about: 🏷 CPITEMLABEL (2026-10-29; RESEARCH §4.8: tree cross section — bark, phloem, cambium, xylem, heartwood): our own drawing of a trunk cut across.

parts.label: Outer bark
parts.words: Protects the tree from weather, insects, fungi, disease and fire

parts.label: Inner bark (phloem)
parts.words: The soft, moist layer under the outer bark that moves food from the leaves down to the rest of the tree

parts.label: Cambium
parts.words: The thin layer of cells under the inner bark where the tree grows: it makes inner bark outward and sapwood inward

parts.label: Sapwood (xylem)
parts.words: The living, lighter wood that carries water and nutrients up from the roots to the crown

parts.label: Heartwood
parts.words: Old, dead cells inside the sapwood, usually darker, that support and strengthen the tree

parts.label: Pith
parts.words: The very center of the trunk

skills.label: Biltmore stick: diameter and height
steps: where to hold it or stand
skills._about: 📏 CPITEMSCALE (2026-10-29; RESEARCH_envirothon_skills_2026-10-28.md §4.9, ranked #9 in §5): read a Biltmore stick drawn on screen — a tree's diameter at breast height, then its height in 16-ft logs from one chain. The stick's marks come from the research's formulas (diameter mark S = √(a·D²/(a+D)), a = reach 25 in; a log mark = 16 × 25 ÷ 66 ≈ 6.1 in; height = logs × 16 + the partial log). A reading counts within tol of the true edge: the nearest whole inch, the nearest half log. Only the stick: the clinometer, prism, pacing, site index and rings are other types or the field day (research §4.9, §6). tests = post-12 (What does DBH stand for?); replaces = the research's §8.1 list for the stick.

data.src: NC Envirothon Forestry Manual pp. 62–65 (the Biltmore stick, logs, DBH); the marks from similar triangles (RESEARCH §4.9)

reads.label: Tree diameter (DBH)
reads.readLbl: Read the stick at the trunk’s right edge: the diameter in inches

ask.label: How high up the trunk do you hold the stick?
ask.why: DBH is the diameter 4½ feet above the ground.
ask.miss: where to hold it — 4½ ft up (breast height)

ask.label: How far from your eye do you hold it?
ask.why: 25 inches, the length of the stick — its marks only read true there.
ask.miss: how far from the eye — 25 inches

reads.label: Tree height in 16-ft logs
reads.readLbl: Read the stick at the top of the usable trunk: how many logs
reads.feetLbl: The usable height in feet (logs × 16, plus 8 for a half log)

ask.label: How far from the tree do you stand?
ask.why: The log marks only read true at 66 feet — one chain.
ask.miss: how far to stand — 66 ft (one chain)

_about_skills: 🧰 CPITEMGEAR (2026-10-29, the class platform's first real skill; RESEARCH_envirothon_skills_2026-10-28.md §4.5, ranked #1 in §5): gear and tool pictures. Each try shows one item's picture from the photo pool (item + tag) and asks what it is, then what it is for. An item with check:true takes its use from field practice, not the MS study documents — Adrienne checks it against the Aquatic Sampling Equipment handout. compile_unit.js checks every skill and lists the items with no photo in the repo set. 📐 CPITEMTRIANGLE (2026-10-29, RESEARCH §4.1, ranked #4 in §5): the USDA soil texture triangle, a `chart` skill with data.kind "ternary". The 12 classes carry the Soil Survey Manual's own rules (rule: OR of ANDs of "<axis or a+b·c>" op value), so the class of any point is exact on every boundary; poly (clay, silt corners) only draws the chart and at places its name. compile_unit.js checks that every point of the triangle (every half percent) falls in exactly ONE class and that the shapes tile it. tests is empty because the triangle questions (2022 Soils Q6, 2026 Soils Q10) are picture questions the app's forms leave out; replaces = the research §8 list (Texture triangle term; Sand and Silt texture class makeup). 🌲 CPITEMID (2026-10-29; RESEARCH_envirothon_skills_2026-10-28.md §4.4, §4.6, §4.7, ranked #5 in §5): ID by part and by sign, with look-alike lures. A try shows one item's photo of ONE part (a tree's leaf, bark, twig or fruit; an animal's track, skull or pelt, or the animal itself) from the photo pool by item + tag, then asks what it shows (the clue, from the item's own ID card: src = <deck>#o<order>) and which item it is — the wrong choices are its look-alikes first (`like`, hand-picked from the research's pairs). A part with no photo in the pool is skipped and listed as needing one.
